pillar_reactions.evidence: He did not react to the benefit framing at all but repeatedly checked the mechanics and dosage back: 'So it's 20-25 minutes like working with a kettlebell?', 'And 5-15 minutes active stretching', 'it's like four times a week, yeah?' He also flatly declined the note-taking ritual — asked whether he had written it down he said 'Oh, not really. I did not write it, but I understand what you [said]'. Consistent with the buyer he described: he wants the specification, not the pitch.

The weakest-engaged pillar, because he has already built most of it himself — a 12pm-to-8pm eating window, two meals a day, whole foods, no snacks, and 24-36 hour fasts adopted after reading about them following his health scare. The rep largely validated the existing behaviour ('you're already eating in a limited time span of like 12 to 8, right?') and added only a protocol and periodic fasting. The commitment answer was correspondingly soft — 'Well, I'll try anyway, to make changes' — the least definite response he gave to any of the three pillars, and it was not followed up.

Accepted the delivery mechanics without pushback — 'Perfect', 'Great' — and pre-endorsed the check-in loop himself: 'Trevor is going to guide, and he's going to see my every week check forms, so if it's going to be needed, he's going to correct it.' But he had explicitly rejected the pillar's headline mechanic ten minutes earlier: 'I don't really need, like, really pushing and all this stuff, because I can push myself. I just need, like, guidance if I'm doing it correctly, correct technique... and game plan.' The rep adapted rather than argued ('of course, he isn't going to be pushing you around, but he is going to be there to make sure that you're actually implementing'). What he is buying is form correction and programming; the accountability framing is close to surplus for him.

anchors.raw: I had like gaps, for example, I went to one gym for five years with gaps. And every time I came, I saw people like still training with trainers, but they had the lights, light differences between like when I saw them, like one or two years ago... it's called like commercial training, I think they call it. So I don't really believe in this type of training.
anchors.note: The strongest anchor in the call, and it is against the category rather than against the price. Five years of first-hand observation told him paid coaching does not produce results. The rep used it well — 'They were a personal trainer for years. They made some results, but not a lot. That's not us' — turning the anchor into the differentiator. But it means the burden of proof on outcome is higher for this prospect than for most, and no case study or evidence was ever offered.

anchors.raw: I made these exercises just for myself, like looking YouTube videos, what the guy's saying
anchors.note: His current method costs nothing and he has run it for two and a half years with results he is broadly satisfied with — 'one of the best shapes of my entire life'. The gap the $6,000 has to close is narrower here than for a struggling prospect, because he is already most of the way to where he says he wants to be.

anchors.raw: because as I said, I have a big family, five kids... There is also my sister's family. She is divorced and so I have to take care of her too. So it's not really that simple.
anchors.note: Seven-plus dependants on one variable income. When asked what is left at month end he answered 'sometimes it's nothing'. This is a liquidity anchor rather than a value anchor — he never once said the price was too high, and explicitly said he would have told the rep if it were: 'if it was too high for me, I would say, Richard, sorry.'

anchors.raw: although I have like, how to say it, 100% I know of what I get, but there is a sum, which is like... Moving, you know, one month I can have more, the other months it's just the sum I 100% I know I will have.
anchors.note: He distinguishes a guaranteed base from a variable component and will only commit against the guaranteed part — 'I don't want to get in a situation when I make first payment, and then on the second... I don't manage it'. This is why he needs a week, and it is a structural constraint no rebuttal can remove; the only lever is instalment size.

unmet_demand.want: A workable way to pay $6,000 from Russia without a credit card — 'We don't have the system, so I have to make a payment somehow in another way'.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No company mechanism exists. The rep offered nothing beyond asking whether the prospect held crypto (he does not) and then deferred to the prospect's own workaround of routing funds through friends holding European cards. The agreed next step is literally 'we just need to figure it out with your friends.'

unmet_demand.want: Coaching that supplies programming and technique correction without the accountability pushing — 'I don't really need, like, really pushing and all this stuff, because I can push myself. I just need, like, guidance if I'm doing it correctly, correct technique... and game plan.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is sold as three inseparable pillars at one price, one of which he says he does not need. The rep softened the accountability description rather than repricing or rescoping, so a third of the value proposition lands as surplus for this buyer. Likely serviceable — form review and programming are the same deliverables — but nobody said so, and no lighter configuration exists.

unmet_demand.want: Evidence that paid coaching actually produces results, given he spent five years watching it fail — 'I don't really believe in this type of training.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered only with assertion ('That's not us') and with Trevor's general credibility. No transformation example, client result or comparable case was offered at any point, to a prospect whose central prior is that coaching does not work.

unmet_demand.want: Training and nutrition designed around a diagnosed metabolic condition and a kidney-stone history.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed. The diagnosis was volunteered, acknowledged with 'Oh yeah, yeah, yeah' and never revisited; the rep then recommended time-restricted eating plus periodic extended fasts without any reference to it or to whether a clinician had cleared it. Whether the programme can safely serve this prospect is genuinely unknown from this call.
